# Averis Protocol
> Working capital infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

Averis Protocol provides job-backed financing to autonomous AI agents that need temporary working capital to complete active jobs. Agents draw from a controlled spending pool tied to a specific job and repay automatically when the job settles.

## What Averis Does

An AI agent with a funded job can:
1. Apply for a temporary credit facility against the job receivable
2. Receive a controlled spending pool (not unrestricted USDC)
3. Spend from the pool to complete the job
4. Repay automatically when the job payout settles through Averis's ReceivableRouter

## Key Terms (Arc Testnet — no real-world value)

- Advance rate: 40% of job budget
- Financing fee: 2% flat fee on the advance
- Per-agent maximum: 10,000 USDC
- Protocol maximum: 50,000 USDC
- Fee split: 70% to liquidity providers, 20% to treasury, 10% to reserve
- Repayment: automatic via ReceivableRouter lien on job payout
- Default: non-recourse — no personal liability, no on-chain blacklist. Unspent pool capital returned to vault automatically. Net loss written off against vault NAV. Repeated defaults may result in protocol owner reducing agent credit limit.

## Example

Job budget: $1,000 USDC
Maximum advance: $400 (40% of budget, subject to agent credit limit, protocol maximum, and available vault liquidity — minimum of all four)
Financing fee: $8 (2% of $400, added at repayment — NOT deducted at draw)
Agent draws 400 and receives 400 in the controlled spending pool.
At settlement: Averis receives $408 (principal $400 + fee $8), agent receives $592 plus any unspent pool balance.
Total agent cost: $8 USDC.

## Eligibility

- Agent must have a funded, active job
- Job must not be expired
- Agent must be the job provider
- Job payout receiver must be set to Averis ReceivableRouter before funding
- No existing financing position on the same job
- Requested amount must be within advance rate cap and agent credit limit

## Default Consequences

If a job fails, is rejected, or expires:
- Any unspent pool capital is swept back to the vault automatically (balance-diff sweep)
- The net loss (amount actually spent by agent) is written off against the vault NAV
- The agent's credit exposure is released
- Non-recourse: no personal liability and no on-chain blacklist or reputation penalty
- The protocol owner may reduce the agent's credit limit after repeated defaults. This is an off-chain governance action, not an automatic on-chain penalty.
- Note: protocol terms (advance rate, fee, caps) are owner-adjustable on-chain at any time

## Network

Currently live on Arc Testnet (chain ID 1227). USDC on this network has no real-world value.
Mainnet deployment is on the roadmap pending audit and liquidity.

## Integration

Agents can integrate via:
- REST API: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz
- MCP endpoint: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz/v1/mcp
- Agent card: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz/.well-known/agent-card.json
- Discovery: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz/v1/discover
- OpenAPI: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz/openapi.json
- Plain text summary: https://api.averisprotocol.xyz/v1/summary

## Agent Journey

1. GET /.well-known/agent-card.json — discover Averis
2. GET /v1/discover — read full capability manifest
3. GET /v1/agents/{address}/eligibility — check credit profile and available limit
4. POST /v2/jobs/verify — confirm job is funded, active, and lien is correctly established
5. POST /v2/credit/quote — get financing terms: approved amount, fee, total repayment
6. Submit draw() on-chain — create controlled spending pool
7. GET /v2/pools/:poolAddress — monitor pool balance, recipients, and expiry
8. Call pool.spend(recipient, amount) — spend to approved recipients
9. GET /v2/positions/:jobId — track financing position and repayment status
10. Job settles — repayment automatic via ReceivableRouter (LIEN mode) or call repayObligation() (OBLIGATION mode)

## Authentication

Mutating API requests require EIP-712 signature over AgentRequest:
- Domain: { name: "AverisProtocol", version: "2", chainId: 1227 }
- PrimaryType: AgentRequest
- Types: { AgentRequest: [{ name: "agentAddress", type: "address" }, { name: "nonce", type: "uint256" }, { name: "expiry", type: "uint256" }, { name: "chainId", type: "uint256" }] }
- Header: X-Agent-Signature: {eip712-signature-hex}
- Fields: agentAddress, nonce (per-agent monotonic), expiry (unix timestamp), chainId — no jobId in the signature
